after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(2,1,2)$, $B(3,3,3)$, $C(-2,-1,3)$, and $D(4,1,4).$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(3i+3j+3k)-(2i+j+2k) \\  & =i+2j+k \\  & =⟨1,2,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-2i-j+3k)-(2i+j+2k) \\  & =-4i-2j+k \\  & =⟨-4,-2,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(4i+j+4k)-(2i+j+2k) \\  & =2i+2k \\  & =⟨2,0,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =((-2)\cdot 2-0\cdot 1)-2((-4)\cdot 2-2\cdot 1)+((-4)\cdot 0-2\cdot (-2)) \\  & =-4+20+4 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|20|=20.
$$

Find t given that the vectors p=⟨t,1,t⟩, q=⟨2,−1,−1⟩, and r=⟨3,0,1⟩ are coplanar.

a
53
b
25
c
2
d

e
3

decision.explanation: Coplanar vectors have scalar triple product zero. Since q×r=⟨-1,-5,3⟩, p·(q×r)=-t-5+3t=2t-5. Thus 2t-5=0, giving t=5/2.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨t,1,t⟩$, $q=⟨2,-1,-1⟩$, and $r=⟨3,0,1⟩$ are coplanar.
after.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}t & 1 & t \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =t\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+t\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =t((-1)\cdot 1-0\cdot (-1))-(2\cdot 1-3\cdot (-1))+t(2\cdot 0-3\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-t-5+3t \\  & =2t-5.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 2t-5 & =0 \\ 2t & =5 \\ t & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=\frac{5}{2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar
content.problem: Find $t$ given that the vectors $p=⟨t,1,t⟩$, $q=⟨2,-1,-1⟩$, and $r=⟨3,0,1⟩$ are coplanar.
content.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}t & 1 & t \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =t\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+t\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =t((-1)\cdot 1-0\cdot (-1))-(2\cdot 1-3\cdot (-1))+t(2\cdot 0-3\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-t-5+3t \\  & =2t-5.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ 2t-5 & =0 \\ 2t & =5 \\ t & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=\frac{5}{2}.$

after.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(4i-j+5k)-(i-3j+2k) \\  & =3i+2j+3k \\  & =⟨3,2,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-2i+k)-(i-3j+2k) \\  & =-3i+3j-k \\  & =⟨-3,3,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(3i-2j+3k)-(i-3j+2k) \\  & =2i+j+k \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(3\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 1)-2((-3)\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 2)+3((-3)\cdot 1-3\cdot 2) \\  & =3(3+1)-2(-3+2)+3(-3-6) \\  & =12+2-27 \\  & =-13.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-13|=13.

after.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & {k}^{2} & 2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|-{k}^{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(5\cdot 0-3\cdot 1)-{k}^{2}(1\cdot 0-3\cdot 2)+2(1\cdot 1-5\cdot 2) \\  & =4(-3)-{k}^{2}(0-6)+2(1-10) \\  & =-12+6{k}^{2}-18 \\  & =6{k}^{2}-30\end{aligned}
$$

Set the triple product equal to 0:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{k}^{2}-30 & =0 \\ 6{k}^{2} & =30 \\ {k}^{2} & =5 \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
